verdicts.note: Tested whether his pledge to 'build on the excellent reputation established by the dedicated staff' [S1] pulls him toward 0. It does not: he has never held elected office [S1] and comes from outside the auditor's office (retiring fire chief, S5) against an appointed incumbent. His long fire-service leadership keeps the magnitude at 1, and medium fits a single pamphlet statement.

S1 says his background 'will strengthen the audit and finance functions while supporting the efficient use of taxpayer dollars' and stresses 'accountability, fiscal responsibility.' That matches pole_a (oversight, audits). It is one clear statement, so medium and magnitude 1 are right.

Tested high confidence against his short tenure (chief deputy from August 2025 [S5], acting auditor from June 2026 [S6]) and his line about 'bringing fresh energy' [S1]. The incumbency is documented in S1 and S6, and S1 explicitly asks to continue Moore's tradition. Short tenure is why the score is -1 and not -2; high confidence in the -1 placement holds.

S1 lists 'protect taxpayer dollars through responsible financial oversight and transparency' as a priority, which matches pole_a. His 2024 line about keeping county government from being 'part of the problem' [S10] leans the same way but is about bureaucracy, not spending, so confidence stays at medium.
